gemini.rationale: The evidence slice states that CCP's customer-facing asset/product tier (T4) crossed into Sabra, but the process/management tier (T5) and organization (T6) did not cross intact, as all CCP executive officers resigned at closing. This creates a structural mismatch between the transferred assets (T4) and the terminated processes/management (T5), resulting in gap_45=1. Since both T5 and T6 were terminated, there is no mismatch between them, so gap_56=0. No transition-services agreement was identified, so the gap was not mitigated.

grok.rationale: gap_45=1 because the slice states CCP’s full 337-property/~37,000-bed customer-facing portfolio crossed into Sabra at the August 17, 2017 closing while ‘the process/management tier did not cross intact’ (all four CCP named executive officers resigned at the effective time under change-in-control provisions and Sabra’s pre-existing senior leadership was to continue running the combined company). gap_56=0 because CCP’s operational processes likewise did not transfer or get re-engineered as a distinct package; they ended with the departing CCP executives, so there was no process-without-organization transfer mismatch—only three non-executive board seats continued. No transaction-specific TSA or shared-services agreement is described that would have contractually absorbed the T4–T5 gap.

openai.rationale: The structural summary states that CCP's 337-property customer-facing portfolio crossed into Sabra, while CCP's process/management tier did not cross intact: all CCP executive officers resigned, and Sabra's existing senior leadership remained in control. This documents a product-versus-process mismatch at closing, supporting gap_45=1; however, the slice does not separately document transferred or re-engineered CCP operational processes lacking an aligned organization, so gap_56=0. No transaction-specific transition-services, shared-services, or external-management agreement was identified, so the documented gap was not contractually mitigated.
